purpose: Detect what BlacksmithGuild must repair or recertify when Bannerlord moves to a new version/build, then emit deterministic sprint candidates.

modes.inventory: Inventory current repo assumptions and produce a baseline packet without requiring a candidate game root or compiling.
modes.candidate: Inspect a candidate Bannerlord root, verify referenced assemblies, run a no-install isolated-output build, reduce compile/dynamic/module/save/certification findings, and produce sprint candidates.
modes.fixture: Reduce deterministic synthetic observations for validator coverage; never claims real candidate compatibility.

findingRules: A missing candidate assembly is a blocker even before compile.
A compiler error against candidate game assemblies is a blocker and must retain file, compiler code, and message when available.
Compile success does not prove reflection, Harmony, string-bound members, UI flow, save loading, or runtime behavior.
Dynamic binding assumptions become explicit review findings on every version-family change unless separately proven against candidate metadata.
A game version/build change invalidates prior save compatibility admission and version-sensitive runtime certification until rerun.
Findings are grouped into sprint candidates by owner lane and dependency; sprint candidates contain an executable first action, expected artifact, and completion gate.
No model may delete, downgrade, or promote a finding without new machine evidence.
allowedScope: read tracked source, project, workflow, test, manifest, and evidence metadata
read candidate Bannerlord files and assembly identities
run dotnet build with candidate GameFolder and isolated temporary output directories
prepare a sanitized GitHub issue draft
publish that issue only through an explicit operator publisher invocation
forbiddenScope: claim candidate runtime compatibility from compile/static proof
automatically create GitHub issues from CI or pre-push
